en.title: Val Gardena snow forecast next week (23–29 November 2026): a minor top-up of 11 cm
en.description: Val Gardena gets 11 cm at the top next week, most of it on 25–26 November. The base receives only 6 cm, suggesting a snow line on the lower slopes.
en.lede: Val Gardena's forecast for 23–29 November centres on 11 cm at the top, 10 cm at mid-mountain and 6 cm at the base. The snow line will sit on the lower slopes, leaving the village to face wet snow or rain as the upper mountain stays cold enough for dry powder.

p: This week (17–20 November) is sparse: 4 cm at 2500 m and barely 1 cm at 1400 m. Next week is the prize. Wednesday 25 and Thursday 26 November carry the bulk of the snow, so if you plan to visit, those days offer the softest turns.

The timing matters because Val Gardena enters this period with little base. Any fresh snow that falls lands on early-season cover, not a deep pack. Early-season avalanche risk depends on how the new layer bonds to what lies beneath; check the regional avalanche bulletin before heading off-piste.

sections.h: Where the snow stops on the mountain
p: The 5 cm gap between the top (11 cm) and the base (6 cm) tells the story of a moving snow line. At 2500 m you get dry powder. By mid-mountain (1900 m) the snow is still solid. Drop to 1400 m and the air is warm enough for wet snow to form, perhaps rain during the day.

The lower runs down to Ortisei, Santa Cristina and Selva in the valley will be first to suffer if temperatures climb. Ski these early in the week if you want them soft; by Sunday 29 November they may turn heavy or patchy.

The Seceda and the Ciampinoi hold snow best, with the shaded Ciampinoi favoured for stable conditions through the week. The Sella Ronda links towards Wolkenstein stay skiable as long as the snow-making has laid its foundation; fresh snow alone is not enough to open a classic loop on early-season cover.
Wednesday 25 November is your best bet: 4 cm at the top with a high forecast of 5 cm. Thursday 26 follows with 4 cm (up to 7 cm). The rest of the week brings flurries only.

The forecast's low case is 5 cm at the top; the high case reaches 18 cm. This wide range reflects the challenge of predicting snow in November, when small shifts in temperature or storm track make large differences. Plan around the central 11 cm, but keep 18 cm in mind as a potential bonus.
The same range applies at mid-mountain (low 4, high 16) and at the base (low 1, high 11). Early-season forecasts carry this spread because the snowpack is thin and sensitive.

Same week, same measurement (top of each resort): Cortina d'Ampezzo 13 cm, Hintertux 14 cm, Obergurgl 13 cm. Val Gardena itself sits at 11 cm—modestly behind but not stranded. The choice between them comes down to terrain preference, not snow depth.
All four resorts face a similar snow line problem: the base lags well behind the summit. No resort in this group has an early-season edge on depth.

sections.h: What this week means for your plan
p: Eleven centimetres at the top is enough to soften the pistes, not enough for a powder holiday. It is a top-up for a mountain that is still building its base. If you are chasing deep snow, Val Gardena is not it this week.

If you are acclimatising to early-season conditions or want groomed runs with a dusting of fresh snow, Wednesday or Thursday offer the best window. We refresh these numbers daily; the Val Gardena page carries the latest forecast.

advice: Fresh snow on a young snowpack brings avalanche risk. Read the regional avalanche bulletin (bollettino valanghe) before any off-piste plan, especially on Wednesday and Thursday when the snowpack is at its heaviest.
Lower runs (Ortisei, Santa Cristina, Selva) will turn to wet snow or slush first if the air warms. Ski them early in the day or early in the week.
The Ciampinoi and Seceda hold snow longest. The shaded Ciampinoi is your best bet for stable conditions through the forecast period.
Opening dates are the resort's decision; our numbers only say how much snow is coming. Confirm lift status before you travel.
With 11 cm at the top, this is not a week to chase powder in Val Gardena. Expect firm pistes with a thin soft top layer on Wednesday and Thursday.
